Keep the same feature coherent across tabs on one browser origin.

People often open the same application twice: a preference changes in one tab, a draft remains open in another, or an administrative view needs the latest committed record. This chapter keeps those Feature State values aligned across same-origin tabs without pretending that every form interaction is shared collaboration.

Why this boundary matters

Tab Sync shares finalized Feature State while each tab retains its own selection, form, loading, and error experience. The behavior and controller coordinate synchronization at the FeatureCell boundary, so the service and component need no special cross-tab plumbing. This is not a substitute for server-authoritative collaboration, cross-device sync, or a security design for sensitive data.

Use this structure for

  • preferences that should remain consistent in every open tab
  • drafts or cart-like State shared within one browser session
  • administrative views that need the latest committed feature value

By the end of this chapter

You will have the Tab Sync behavior and controller configured as a pair, with finalized character State updating across same-origin tabs while transient page interactions remain local to each tab.

Chapter 12 Starting Point and Synchronization Scope

Start with the completed Chapter 11 project. Tab Sync is a Pro capability; production use requires a valid license. This lab changes configuration, component presentation, and tests. The service does not add cross-tab messaging code.

Shared vs. Local
  • Shared: finalized FeatureCell value identified by the same key on the same origin—scheme, host, and port.
  • Local: selection, unsaved form values, pending confirmation, loading, and error presentation in each tab.
  • Not provided: server authority, authorization, cross-device sync, offline reconciliation, audit history, or collaborative conflict resolution.
Concurrent Edits Need a Product Policy

This lab demonstrates propagation, not transactional consistency. Do not infer a winner or ordering guarantee from sequential edits. This tutorial deliberately defines no simultaneous-write contract: Tab Sync transports finalized Feature State but does not reconcile record-level conflicts. Before production use, choose server-owned versions, ETags, or another explicit policy for simultaneous edits, stale forms, and server rejection.

Environment Support Checklist
  • Both tabs use the same scheme, host, port, and FeatureCell key.
  • The browser permits the required storage and messaging mechanism.
  • Private or restricted contexts may disable the demonstration.
  • The browser allows the second tab to open and both pages remain active.
  • Reload both tabs after correcting configuration; do not copy State manually.

Step 45: Configure Tab Sync

↑ top

Tab Sync keeps one State value aligned across browser tabs that share the same origin. You configure the complete feature in app.config.ts: the State behavior shares finalized values, and the controller coordinates the initial State when you open another tab.

Register both on the same . The behavior belongs in the behaviors array and the controller belongs in the controllers array passed to provideFeatureCell(). Nothing changes in the service or component to make synchronization work.

Make the Change
  1. Open the app.config.ts file.
  2. Import withTabSyncStateBehavior and withTabSyncController from .
  3. Add the behavior to the behavior list and the controller to the controller list for the same .
What to Look For
  • The behavior and controller are a required pair for this FeatureCell.
  • The configuration owns cross-tab State coordination; the service and component stay focused on their existing responsibilities.
  • Only finalized FeatureCell State is shared with a peer tab.
What the Stale-Form Exercise Proves

The exercise proves only that a peer's committed collection can update while Tab B's unsaved form remains local. It does not prove that saving the stale form is safe or define which concurrent write wins. Cancel the stale form in this lab. In production, compare a server-owned version before accepting the save.

Step 46: View Tab Sync

↑ top

Select View Tab Sync to open this example in a new browser tab. Make a character change in either tab and watch the committed collection update in the other tab. The button only opens the second tab; the registered behavior and controller perform all State synchronization.

Local-State Demonstration

The stale-form exercise intentionally contrasts synchronized committed State with unsynchronized draft state. Cancel the local draft after the peer update; do not save it as though it were based on the new record.

Run and Verify
  1. Select View Tab Sync to open a second tab.
  2. Add, edit, delete, or reset a character collection in either tab.
  3. Return to the other tab and inspect the synchronized character State.
  4. Leave an unsaved edit open in Tab B, commit a change in Tab A, and confirm the committed collection updates while Tab B's transient form remains local. Cancel the stale form before continuing.
Troubleshooting

If the second tab does not update, confirm both pages have the same origin and FeatureCell key, allow the browser to open the new tab, and verify both the behavior and controller are registered. Private-browsing or restricted storage/messaging policies can prevent the demonstration. After correcting the cause, reload both tabs to re-establish the initial handshake and retry one committed update.

What to Look For
  • Committed FeatureCell State values are preserved and updated between tabs, including shared resets.
  • Forms, selection, loading, errors, and other page interactions remain local to the tab where they occur.
  • A failed pipeline attempt does not update a peer tab.
  • The new tab receives State without inheriting transient loading or error metadata from its peer.
